voiceBand: §16 Beginner (bands 2-4, default). Provisional: confirm at pathway pressure-test.

shapes.quote: Broadly speaking, this type of learning is focused on professional practice; it involves the application of theory or knowledge learnt in classroom settings to the way you do something, whether you're a student nurse or teacher, or you're an artist developing your craft.
In the list below, we've tried to highlight the main ones.

cards.tierBrief: Introduce the topic from first principles and bridge from prior (school/college) experience; concrete and reassuring.
cards.baseContent: Orient the learner to this lesson's topic: what it is, why it matters, and what the lesson will look at; bridge from what they already know.

cards.tierBrief: Start of the degree / first year: the ways of working are new; the learner is not expected to have mastered them yet; they are finding their feet. Reassuring and normalising.
cards.baseContent: Position the lesson for where the learner is in their studies: what is and is not expected of them at this level, normalising the stage they are at.

cards.tierBrief: Bloom floor: identify, describe, recognise, use.
cards.baseContent: Present this lesson's outcomes decided at crs-04; do not invent them. Each serves exactly one course outcome (AL-1); one verb, one object (AL-2).

cards.tierBrief: Define from first principles in plain terms: one clear idea with a concrete example; avoid jargon and caveats.
cards.baseContent: Define the lesson's concept plainly, example-first where it helps; the generic definition the context pack's concept-context follows on from.

cards.tierBrief: One concrete example of the concept in the subject; plain, two or three sentences.
cards.baseContent: A short follow-on from the generic concept-definition, showing the concept in the learner's own subject; the context pack supplies the whole prose.

cards.tierBrief: A recognition or sorting task at the level of the basic concept; unambiguous, with one clear right grouping.
cards.baseContent: The lesson's interactive concept activity: the task itself teaches the concept (learn by doing), authored generically.
cards.authoringPrompt: Activity mode — the task itself teaches the concept. For a manipulation question (matching/sortable/hotspot/slider): plausible, unambiguous options/pairs/targets; incorrect feedback (notFinal) explains and points toward the answer; correct feedback restates the concept, not a bare verdict. Balance any selected options per docs/authoring/mcq-authoring-guidance.md.

cards.tierBrief: A simple, single-point contrast: one clear thing the stronger version does better, in an everyday situation.
cards.baseContent: A third-person worked example showing the concept in use: a weaker attempt first, then a stronger one reached by better practice, with the cast named directly.
cards.authoringPrompt: Worked example — third person: a weaker/less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice; make explicit what the stronger one does differently.

cards.tierBrief: First, concrete habits to start now; few steps, low overhead; reassure that starting small is right.
cards.baseContent: Practical, do-this-now guidance the learner can act on this week; why before how; concrete steps, not restated theory.
cards.authoringPrompt: Practical, do-this-now guidance the learner can act on this week; why-before-how; concrete steps, not restated theory.

cards.tierBrief: Test recognition and recall of the basic concept; distractors are common everyday misconceptions.
cards.baseContent: A question testing one lesson outcome, with teaching feedback - never a bare right/wrong.
cards.authoringPrompt: Author MCQ options balanced per docs/authoring/mcq-authoring-guidance.md: all options the same length and specificity so the correct answer is never the longest or most qualified; distractors are plausible misconceptions, not filler; keep hedging and absolutes even across options; feedback gives the reason, never a bare verdict.

cards.tierBrief: Ask the learner to notice their own habits and first reactions; gentle, concrete, low-stakes.
cards.baseContent: One to three genuine open questions with no right answers; private, unmarked tone; invite the learner's own view, never quiz.
cards.authoringPrompt: 1-3 genuine open questions with no right answers; private, unmarked tone; invite the learner's own view, never quiz.

cards.tierBrief: Affirm the first concrete capabilities and encourage; point to the next lesson or step. Keep it foundational.
cards.baseContent: Recap what the learner can now do, outcome by outcome, and why it matters next; affirm progress; introduce no new content.
cards.authoringPrompt: Recap what the learner can now do, outcome by outcome, and why it matters next; affirm progress; introduce no new content.

cards.tierBrief: Same pointer form regardless of subject; a bySubject or byInstitution steer, once set, may override the referencing style (Harvard / APA / OSCOLA).
cards.baseContent: List this lesson's real sources as footnote-style pointers (LSP-1): 'See pages x to y of Chapter n of *Title* by Authors', citing at least the chapter and page range.
cards.authoringPrompt: Footnote-style pointer(s) only — 'See pages x-y of Chapter n of Title by Authors'; chapter + page range; real sources only (LSP-1).
